Launchpad research · November 1, 2026

The 0.0016%: what survives a memecoin launchpad

Of 24,563,926 tokens launched on pump.fun, 390 are alive above $100k today, about 1 in 62,984. This report studies those survivors: who they are, how they got there, who made money trading them, and how other launchpads compare. Snapshot October 31, 2026; every number is computed from on-chain and market data or cited.

1. Summary

  • 390 survivors out of 24.6M launches (0.0016%). 118 are above $1M, 17 above $10M and one (Fartcoin) above $100M. The median survivor is $402k: most sit just over the line.
  • The typical token never gets going. Across 19.2M pump.fun tokens Dune can see, the median lifetime volume is $1k and the median token trades on 1 day. Only 1% ever pass $227k of volume.
  • Graduation is about 1 in 116 in a normal stretch (0.86%), recently inflated to 2.95% by July's BOOST incentive change, much of it self-funded.
  • Once past $100k, survivors stay there. The median survivor closed at $100k or more on 99% of its days since graduating; 280 of 389 did on at least 90% of them.
  • Two kinds of survivor. 187 of 389 have traded for over a year (median age 348 days), while 43 are under 30 days old and have not yet faced the test of time.
  • Even in the winners, 59% of trading positions are under water (realized + unrealized). The top 1% of positions hold 82% of all profit.
  • Creator rewards are real but thin. $649.38M has accrued to pump.fun creators since May 2025, but the median token earned $0.55. The 368 survivors with measurable fees took 3.8% of it; their median creator earned $18k.
  • Pons, for comparison. On Robinhood Chain, 98 of ~646k Pons launches are above $100k (0.015%, about 1 in 6,592), a rate roughly 10× pump.fun's, from a far younger and smaller base.

Staying above $100k

  • The median survivor closed at $100k or more on 287 days, 99% of its days since graduation (median 336 days since graduating). A quarter are at 88% or less.
  • Whole days, not just closes: counting only days when even the day's low held $100k, the median is still 98%. 280 of 389 survivors closed at $100k or more on at least 90% of their post-graduation days; 26 spent most of them below.
  • How to read it: survivors don't hover around $100k. Once past it, they mostly stay. These are tokens alive today, so this says nothing about the tokens that crossed $100k and later died.
  • How it is measured: daily open, high, low and close market cap for each survivor from every Dune trade of $10 or more across all venues, × 1B supply. Daily high and low use the 99th/1st percentile trade price, so one mispriced swap can't set the range. A day with no trades counts as below. On the 82,948 days both sources cover, Dune and GeckoTerminal agree 99.9% on whether the close was ≥$100k.

6. Who made money trading the survivors

Read this as survivorship bias, on purpose. These are trades in 389 of the 390 tokens still alive above $100k (one has no trade history on Dune): about 0.0016% of everything launched. Trades in the other 99.998% were not measured; most of those tokens are worth close to nothing. So the question is not "do memecoin traders make money" but "even in the winners, who made money?"

  • The whole platform: $649.38M in creator fees accrued from May 13, 2025 (when creator fees began) to Nov 1, 2026, across 13.7M tokens: $545.68M on PumpSwap and $103.70M on the bonding curve. The median token earned its creator $0.55; the 99th percentile $349. 461 tokens earned over $100k; none over $1M (largest $628k).
  • Survivors: the 368 survivors with measurable fees accrued $24.93M, 3.8% of all creator fees, from about 0.0016% of tokens. Median $18k, 90th percentile $231k; 81 earned over $100k. 118 earned nothing: all first traded before creator fees began (May 13, 2025). Another 21 launched later but trade against USDC or other tokens, whose creator fees are not measured here; they are left out of the fee figures.
  • How it is measured: fees accrued per token in Dune's decoded pump.fun events: bonding-curve trades quoted in SOL and PumpSwap pools quoted in WSOL, priced at the daily SOL price. It counts fees whoever received them (the original creator, a later creator address, or fee-sharing recipients). Dune's older event format (bonding curve, before about Nov 2025) has no fee fields, so $30.49M (5% of the total) is estimated from volume at pump.fun's published curve rate. Curves quoted in other tokens (2.7% of bonding-curve trades) are left out. Cross-check: DefiLlama puts PumpSwap's fees to LPs and creators at $798M over the same period, of which our $545.68M creator share is a plausible part, and its bonding-curve figure ($126M) is close to ours ($103.70M).

9. Platform trends

  • Revenue: ~$1.55B lifetime (Dune). DefiLlama: $321M in 2024 and $649M in 2025.
  • Daily launches: peaked at 71,735 (Jan 23, 2025); September 2026 averaged ~33k a day, with 36–52k a day in late October.
  • Market share: pump.fun created 78% of new Solana tokens (Nov 2025 – Oct 2026, peaking at 90% in Aug 2026). LetsBonk briefly flipped it in Jul 2025.
  • PUMP buybacks: ~$350–400M cumulative; 50% of net revenue now funds buyback-and-burn.

The other side. Bundling is not automatically malicious: a visible, disclosed dev buy at launch is the on-chain version of a team allocation, and Bubblemaps treats bundled supply under 5% as low concern. What hurts buyers is hidden concentration. Trader outcomes also improved in 2026: CoinGecko's profitable-wallet share rose from 30% (Jun 2025) to 73% (Apr 2026).

12. Methodology and sources

  • Survivors: mints ending in "pump" priced ≥$100k on DexScreener with ≥$5k liquidity and liquidity ≥1.5% of market cap, from the top 1,500 coins by market cap in CoinGecko's Pump.fun category plus the top 400 PumpSwap/pump.fun pools on GeckoTerminal by volume and by trade count. Also required: at least 50 holders and lifetime volume of at least 5% of market cap, which removes 3 fake-valuation tokens. Early pump.fun tokens without the suffix (MOODENG, ZEREBRO, GRIFFAIN…) are excluded; CoinGecko's category counts 441 above $100k when they are included.
  • Survivor history: Dune dex_solana.trades across every Solana DEX venue (pump.fun's curve, PumpSwap, Raydium, Meteora, Orca and others). Volume counts each swap leg, including aggregator hops and arbitrage bots, so it is higher than single-pool figures; it is measured the same way for every token. Daily market cap = daily volume-weighted price × 1B supply; peak = the highest of those, or today's market cap if higher. Current market cap, liquidity and 24h volume come from the DexScreener snapshot; holders and top-10 share from GeckoTerminal. GeckoTerminal serves only about a year of daily candles, so it was not used for age or lifetime volume.
  • Trader P&L: per wallet and token, from every swap in Dune's trade table, using the position's lifetime average buy cost (not a running average, so the split between realized and unrealized is approximate; the total is not affected). Realized = sell proceeds − tokens sold × average buy cost; unrealized = tokens held now × (Oct 31 snapshot price − average buy cost), with holdings read from Dune's latest on-chain balances. Transfer check: a wallet that only swapped holds exactly what it bought minus what it sold. Positions whose real balance differs from that by more than 5% of what they swapped moved tokens by plain transfer and are left out of the headline, as are wallets that never bought by swap. Swap fees and Solana network fees are not deducted. One person running many wallets counts as many wallets; one wallet holding for many people (a bot or exchange) counts as one.
  • Creator rewards: Dune decoded pump.fun events (pumpdotfun_solana.pump_evt_tradeevent creator_fee; pump_amm_evt_buyevent/sellevent coin_creator_fee, pools mapped to tokens via pump_amm_evt_createpoolevent), SOL-quoted only, priced at the daily SOL average. Accrued, not claimed. Bonding-curve trades before about Nov 2025 are estimated from volume (see below). Cross-check against on-chain creator-vault inflows (Helius) for the 168 survivors with a measurable vault: 61 match within 20%, many to the SOL; 106 are higher on Dune because fees went to fee-sharing or later creator addresses the original vault never saw; 1 lower.
  • Dune is missing pump.fun's first months. Dune's trade table starts on 2024-05-30, but pump.fun launched in January 2024. It shows about 19.4M pump.fun mints trading on pump.fun's curve, PumpSwap or Raydium (19.2M with a USD-priced trade) against 24.6M launched, so about 5M are absent: tokens from before May 30, 2024, and tokens that never had a priced trade. It shows 156,828 pump.fun tokens trading on Raydium and 236,298 on PumpSwap (from 2025-03-14). The "reached a DEX pool" group means any token that traded on PumpSwap or Raydium, which includes tokens that created their own pool without graduating, so it is larger than the graduation count. Every all-token statistic means "tokens that traded on or after 2024-05-30".
  • Creator fees and Dune's older event format: Dune decodes pump.fun bonding-curve trades before about November 2025 in an older format with no fee fields. For those trades, creator fees are estimated from SOL volume at pump.fun's published curve creator rate (0.05% until Sep 2, 2025; 0.30% after, which matches the decoded fees once they appear). PumpSwap creator fees are decoded throughout.
  • Platform series: Dune dashboard adam_tehc/pumpfun (launches, graduations, revenue); DefiLlama (revenue, volume).
  • Pons: tokens with pools tracked on GeckoTerminal, with the same thresholds as pump.fun (≥$5k liquidity and liquidity ≥1.5% of market cap), though the pump.fun list is built from CoinGecko and GeckoTerminal top lists. The launch count (~646k) is from Sep 3, 2026 (CoinDesk); launches since then would lower Pons's rate, so the comparison is an upper bound.
  • Survivorship: the survivor sections describe tokens alive now. Millions of dead tokens that once reached these levels are not in them.
